learningObjective: Reason about cross compilation in the ML compilation stack: compiling on a host machine for a target device that differs in ISA, GPU architecture, or OS.

canonicalClaims.claim: Cross compilation produces artifacts on a host machine for a different target (ISA/GPU arch/OS). It relies on the compiler supporting the target back-end and typically uses static cost models or offline-recorded autotune tables when the target is unavailable for online measurement; portable IR (PTX, SPIR-V) with driver-time JIT is another strategy.
conditions: The target back-end is supported by the toolchain.
Target hardware may or may not be available during build.
nonImplications: Does not imply cross-compiled performance always matches native compilation.
Does not imply autotuning is impossible offline; some stacks record per-target measurements.

misconceptions.claim: NVCC can only emit code for the host GPU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: NVCC supports emitting PTX and SASS for a list of specified sm_XX targets.

misconceptions.claim: Autotuning can be replaced by static cost models with zero performance loss.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Static models are approximations; loss depends on how well they generalize to the target.

misconceptions.claim: PTX is target-specific and cannot be used for cross compilation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PTX is a portable IR that the driver JITs to the target SASS; that's why it enables cross compilation and forward compatibility.

misconceptions.claim: Cross compilation is only relevant for embedded targets.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It also applies to CI/CD pipelines building for cloud GPUs from a different developer machine.
